text:
Where fear does not tell tales and poems, does not form figures of terror and glory.


Gray emptiness is my name, my pronoun.


I know the range of fears and that beginning to sing softly in the ravine that leads back toward the unknown woman I am, my emigrant from herself.


I write against fear. Against the clawed wind that lodges in my breathing.


And when in the morning you fear finding yourself dead (and that there are no more images): the silence of understanding, the silence of mere being, in this the years go by, in this the lovely animal joy went away.

translation.title: Where Fear Does Not Tell Tales and Poems...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the prose density and the shifting self-address in the source.
